solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put a coat on and disappear round corner at last

indicators.note: one word is placed round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to disappear is to vanish

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word corner

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put on a coat and slip away round the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a coat on' looks like dressing; it is the definition, as in painting. 'round' puts VANISH around R, the last letter of 'corner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying varnish means brushing a protective glossy coat onto wood or another surface.

clue.text: Element of technical language judge avoided

indicators.note: avoided means the judge's letter is left out of the word

parts.note: jargon is the specialist vocabulary of a trade

explanation.surface: A judge steers clear of a bit of technical language in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoided' removes J from JARGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble gas, chemical element number 18, found in small amounts in the air.

parts.note: one sense of present: the present moment, this very time
the other sense of present: present in this place, not absent

explanation.surface: Two gifts have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like gifts, but means two senses of being present, in time and in place. The definition is a cryptic hint: something nowhere to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Something located in no place at all cannot be found by anyone searching.

definitions.meaning: a collection of things belonging together
prepared, as in all ... to go

explanation.surface: A band announces it is ready to play.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a collection of matching items and being prepared to start.

parts.note: Del is the delete key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman holds a key part, perhaps the musical key of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a musical key such as D, but it is the computer key Del.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, borne for instance by the British singer, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Small drink before a 23, for instance

indicators.note: before places the drink ahead of the single letter in the answer

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, especially whisky

explanation.surface: Having a nip of whisky before a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 23 across is a Shakespeare tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is a play, and a play is an example of the theatrical genre.

clue.text: Litre, for example? Not so much drunk

parts.note: less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A litre of drink, perhaps, leaves one not quite so drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: LEGLESS is British slang for very drunk, too drunk to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for extremely intoxicated, as if unable to stand on one's own feet.

clue.text: How fireworks are a great success?

definitions.text: How fireworks are a great success?

parts.words: How fireworks are a great success?
parts.note: fireworks literally finish with an explosion, and the idiom for a striking success uses that very phrase

explanation.surface: Asking what makes a firework display a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being a resounding success is literally what fireworks do.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be a great success, and fireworks do so literally by exploding loudly.

clue.text: Tricky week in a section of hospital

indicators.note: in places the week abbreviation inside the other letters

parts.note: a ward is a room or division of a hospital

explanation.surface: A difficult week spent on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the container; the week's abbreviation sits after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward and tricky are synonyms for something hard to handle or deal with.

indicators.note: the word manner loses both its end letters, keeping only its inner ones

explanation.surface: A queen's behaviour is moderate, never going to extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing no extremes' drops the outer M and R of 'manner'. Anne was Queen of Great Britain 1702-1714.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Anne was the last Stuart monarch, reigning in the early eighteenth century.

clue.text: Sit down to steal from church?

definitions.meaning: an informal invitation to be seated
to take one of the benches from a church, read literally

explanation.surface: An invitation to sit, or a joking question about stealing church furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom invites someone to take a seat; literally it means walking off with a church bench.

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the words are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Oddly, Gill's phone is not ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges GILL NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells tolling are ringing slowly and repeatedly, as for a funeral.

parts.note: a swell is an old word for a fashionable man about town

explanation.surface: Someone else is a dandy too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' is old-fashioned slang for a dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean also or in addition.

clue.text: Sort of heater that is so great when repaired

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters are put back together in a fixed new order

explanation.surface: A type of heater that works so well once mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when repaired' rearranges SO GREAT. A storage heater, common in Britain, stores cheap night-time electricity as heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A storage heater is an electric radiator that holds heat and releases it later.

parts.note: at can mean next to, as in at the door
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Standing still alongside everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Being still and motionless is to be resting, without movement.

clue.text: No way hiding, ready for quick thrust

indicators.note: hiding means one word conceals the others inside it

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat
O, nought, means none
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: There is no way to hide when someone is ready for a quick attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' marks the container. 'No' as the letter O (nought) and 'way' as street are standard crossword abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing, a riposte is a swift return thrust after parrying, and figuratively a sharp retort.

clue.text: Divine baby one accepts responsibility for

parts.note: a divine being is a god
a baby is a young child

explanation.surface: A sacred infant whom someone takes into their care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective describing the baby, but it gives a noun, GOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent accepts responsibility for the religious upbringing of a child at its baptism.

indicators.note: damaged suggests the word is broken and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Food is salvaged from a broken packing case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges CRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Caterers supply and serve meals for events, so to provide meals is to cater.

indicators.note: turning means the word up is read backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A cat appears alongside its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses UP to give PU.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma, also called cougar or mountain lion, is a large American wild cat.

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other word

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: A daughter breaks into dinner as the gong sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' looks like the dinner gong; it is British slang for an award or decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is informal British slang for a decoration or award, especially a military one.

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stoned a second time grows very irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadfully' rearranges STONED AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise someone is to provoke their hostility, making them irritated.

clue.text: Crazy person that may be going to bolt

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a madman or lunatic

definitions.text: that may be going to bolt
definitions.meaning: a threaded fastener screwed onto a bolt

explanation.surface: A mad person who might run away at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' suggests running off, but here it is the metal fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a madman, and the small threaded fastener that screws onto a bolt.

indicators.note: with joins the fruit to the letter that follows it in the answer

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit with a big stone in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' looks like a fruit stone, but it means a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is counted among the precious gems, which are loosely called stones.

indicators.note: back means the little word to is reversed

parts.note: hello is a greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A tragic hero is welcomed back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses TO to give OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor of Venice is the title character of one of his great tragedies.
